title: bug: candidate archive test assumes GNU tar owner/group format and fails on Windows bsdtar
description:
Reproduced before any edits on task-b2b4550835f14b6ebd4a742e1f3b01cf, HEAD2e4ff607 shared tree: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test exits1 solely at apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-archive.test.ts:66.
Assertion expects '1000/1000', but native tar -tv emits distinct '1000   1000' columns for both USTAR entries; full evidence in parent comment-5a9bee5feded41a0b263e23bc119094e. Preserve numeric ownership and exact entry checks without hard-coding GNU listing layout.
definitionOfDone: The native tar archive test passes on Windows bsdtar without weakening its numeric uid/gid or exact-entry assertions; tests cover supported GNU and BSD listing shapes or inspect the actual archive numeric fields independently.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test exits0 and records positive Test Files/Tests count lines; any unrelated failures are disclosed with paths.

implementationPlan.description:
REPRODUCE THROUGH THE TEST, NOT THROUGH YOUR SHELL. NO EDITS.

Run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (or the single file) and confirm it exits 1 at apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-archive.test.ts:66. Quote the failing assertion verbatim into a row comment — that is the pre-fix red this row's evidence rests on.

DO NOT REPRODUCE BY RUNNING `tar` IN GIT BASH. It will pass and you will wrongly conclude the row is stale. `readBack` at :30-33 calls `spawnSync("tar", [...], { shell: false })`, and with shell:false on Windows Node resolves `tar` off PATH to `C:\Windows\System32\tar.exe` — **bsdtar**, not the GNU tar Git Bash provides. Measured at plan time:
  GNU tar 1.35:  `-rw-r--r-- Yaron/197121      1 2026-09-09 22:33 a.txt`   (owner/group joined by a SLASH)
  bsdtar 3.8.8:  `-rw-rw-rw-  0 0      0           1 Sep 09 22:33 a.txt`   (SEPARATE space-separated columns)
That difference is the entire defect.

THEN READ THE THING THAT DECIDES THE FIX: :228-243, in the `"the header checksum is the one a reader recomputes"` block, ALREADY inspects the archive's own numeric fields — `Number.parseInt(field(at, 108, 8), 8)` and `field(at, 116, 8)` asserted to be 1000 for BOTH header blocks, with literals, and :234 pinning the constants separately. So the numeric ownership guarantee does not depend on any listing format and is already stated more strictly than :66. DoD 1's second branch is therefore already satisfied, and the work is DoD 1's first branch only.

While you are there, note what :66's arm uniquely provides and must keep: that a REAL tar, reading these bytes, reports those ids.

implementationPlan.description:
MAKE THE ONE ASSERTION FORMAT-TOLERANT WITHOUT LOOSENING IT (:66).

Replace `expect(listed.out).toContain("1000/1000")` with a pattern that accepts BOTH real layouts — GNU's `1000/1000` and bsdtar's `1000` and `1000` in adjacent whitespace-separated columns — while still requiring BOTH numbers to be exactly 1000 and ADJACENT to each other. Something of the shape `/(?:^|\s)1000[/\s]+1000(?:\s|$)/mu`; the exact spelling is yours, the requirement is not.

KEEP THE LITERALS. The comment at :64-65 explains why and it is right: "Literal, not the imported constant: a constant on both sides of the assertion moves with the mutation and stays green." Do not reach for ARCHIVE_OWNER_UID here.

WHAT THE PATTERN MUST NOT ADMIT, and this is the whole difference between a fix and a weakening: a listing showing uid 1000 with gid 0. That is a real delivery failure — a root-group 0600 file is unreadable by the app user and surfaces 150 seconds later as a health timeout naming nothing. `toContain("1000")` and `/1000.*1000/` both admit it; neither is acceptable.

UPDATE THE COMMENT at :64-65 to say why the pattern is shaped this way: two real tars print the same fact in two layouts, GNU joins them with a slash and bsdtar prints separate columns, and the arm accepts both while still pinning both numbers. A future reader who sees a regex where a literal was will otherwise assume it was loosened for convenience.

CHANGE NOTHING ELSE IN THE ARM. :67's `-rw-------` and :68-69's entry-name check both survive under bsdtar — the split at :68 consumes CRLF and `.pop()` takes the last token regardless of column count or date format. If :67 also fails on the host, it is the same class of defect and belongs in this row; fix it the same way and say so.
implementationPlan.note:
:66 IS NOW FORMAT-TOLERANT WITHOUT BEING LOOSER.

Added module-level `APP_USER_OWNS_THE_LISTED_ENTRY = /(?<![\d/])1000[/ \t]+1000(?![\d/])/u` above the describe, with a doc comment carrying BOTH measured layouts verbatim and the reason for the shape. :66 changed from `expect(listed.out).toContain("1000/1000")` to `expect(listed.out).toMatch(APP_USER_OWNS_THE_LISTED_ENTRY)`. Comment at :64-65 rewritten to point at that constant.

WHY THE LOOKAROUND FORM RATHER THAN THE PLAN'S SKETCH `(?:^|\s)...(?:\s|$)/mu`: `\s` matches a NEWLINE, so the sketch can straddle two listing lines (a line ending in 1000 followed by a line starting with 1000). `[/ \t]+` cannot leave the line, and `(?<![\d/])`/`(?![\d/])` are digit boundaries that also reject a slash on the outside — which is what keeps `11000/10001` out. Same requirement, tighter.

WHAT IT ACCEPTS/REFUSES (proved by the arm landing in step 3): accepts GNU `1000/1000` and bsdtar `1000   1000`; refuses `1000/1001` and `1000      0` (the uid-1000/gid-0 delivery failure) and `11000/10001`.

1000s stayed LITERAL — ARCHIVE_OWNER_UID/GID deliberately not referenced here.

NOTHING ELSE IN THE ARM TOUCHED. :67 `-rw-------` and :68-69 entry names both already survive bsdtar (measured in step 1), so no fix was needed there.

VERIFIED ON BOTH REAL TARS, same command, PATH the only difference:
  PowerShell (bsdtar 3.8.8): Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 13 passed (13), EXIT=0  [was 1 failed | 12 passed]
  Git Bash  (GNU tar 1.35): Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 13 passed (13), EXIT=0  [unchanged]

implementationPlan.description:
PROVE THE TOLERANCE IS NOT A LOOSENING (the arm DoD 1 implies but does not spell out).

Add a small arm that runs the new pattern against FIXED LISTING STRINGS and asserts what it accepts and what it refuses. No tar involved — this is about the pattern, and hard-coded sample lines make it deterministic on every host:
- ACCEPTS a GNU-shaped line carrying `1000/1000`.
- ACCEPTS a bsdtar-shaped line carrying `1000` and `1000` in adjacent columns.
- REFUSES `1000/1001` and `1000    0` — the mismatched-gid cases, which are the real failures this arm exists to keep catching.
- REFUSES a line carrying `11000/10001`, so the pattern is not matching a substring of a longer number.

This is the arm that makes the regex honest. Without it, "tolerant of both shapes" and "asserts nothing in particular" look identical in a diff, and the next reviewer has no way to tell which one landed.

Name the arm for the property, not the mechanism — it is about which ownership a listing may report, not about a regular expression.
implementationPlan.note:
ARM LANDED AND PROVEN NON-VACUOUS. Full counterfactual source + results in comment-cd7e9713ca6b4796bc99d486dd1fc6ec.

New arm, named for the property: "reads the app user's ownership out of either tar's layout, and only when BOTH ids are it". Both ACCEPT lines are real measured output off this archive, not composed. Asserts against the SAME production constant the listing arm uses (APP_USER_OWNS_THE_LISTED_ENTRY) — not a copy.

ACCEPTS: GNU `1000/1000`; bsdtar `1000   1000`.
REFUSES: `1000/1001`; bsdtar gid 0; `11000/10001`; `10001000`; a same-line uid-1000/gid-0 entry whose SIZE is 1000; a two-line listing pairing one entry's uid with the next entry's gid. Plus a guard asserting the string replacements actually fired, so the refusals cannot go vacuous.

THE COUNTERFACTUAL CHANGED THE DELIVERY TWICE — it was not a rubber stamp. My first arm carried only the plan's four cases; two genuinely WEAKER patterns passed it: `/(?<![\d/])1000[\s\S]+1000(?![\d/])/u` (arbitrary text, incl. newlines, between the ids) and the `*`-for-`+` variant (admits the 8-digit id `10001000`). The last three assertions above were added to close both. 5 of 6 loosenings now red the arm; `/1000/u` — the shape a careless "fix" would reach for — fails 6 of 8 checks.

ONE SURVIVOR, DISCLOSED NOT PAPERED OVER: the plan's own sketch `/(?:^|\s)1000[/\s]+1000(?:\s|$)/mu` passes all eight. Mine is strictly tighter (its `[/\s]+` crosses newlines, my `[/ \t]+` cannot) but they diverge only on a listing where two 1000s are separated by nothing but whitespace across lines, which no real tar emits. I did not manufacture an unrealistic assertion to kill it.

NO ON-DISK MUTATION AT ANY POINT. full-suite-gate is HELD by worker-b42eccd4 (task-161b7e9d, ten-leg regression) since 17:14:26Z with two rows queued; drilling a file its suite may read is what the rail forbids. ACCEPTED — make the ONE format-dependent assertion tolerant of both real tars, and prove the tolerance is not a loosening with a negative control. DoD 1 offers two routes and the first is the right one here, because the second is ALREADY DONE elsewhere in the same file (see codebaseInsights).

REJECTED — relax the assertion to `toContain("1000")`. That is precisely the weakening DoD 1 forbids: it would pass on a listing showing uid 1000 and gid 0, which is a real delivery failure (a root-group 0600 file is unreadable by the app user).

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
THE CAUSE, measured on this host rather than inferred. `readBack` at :30-33 calls `spawnSync("tar", [...], { shell: false })`. With shell:false on Windows, Node resolves `tar` off PATH to `C:\Windows\System32\tar.exe`, which is **bsdtar 3.8.8 / libarchive**, NOT the GNU tar that Git Bash provides. I ran both:
  GNU tar 1.35:   `-rw-r--r-- Yaron/197121      1 2026-09-09 22:33 a.txt`
  bsdtar 3.8.8:   `-rw-rw-rw-  0 0      0           1 Sep 09 22:33 a.txt`
GNU joins owner and group with a SLASH; bsdtar prints them as SEPARATE space-separated columns. So `expect(listed.out).toContain("1000/1000")` at :66 can only pass under GNU tar. That is the whole defect and it is one line.

THE PROPERTY IS ALREADY PROVEN INDEPENDENTLY, WHICH DECIDES THE FIX. The `"the header checksum is the one a reader recomputes"` block already inspects the archive's own numeric fields:
  :242 `expect(Number.parseInt(field(at, 108, 8), 8)).toBe(1000);`  // uid at USTAR offset 108
  :243 `expect(Number.parseInt(field(at, 116, 8), 8)).toBe(1000);`  // gid at USTAR offset 116
for BOTH header blocks (`for (const at of [0, ARCHIVE_BLOCK_BYTES])`), with LITERAL 1000s, and :234 pins `[ARCHIVE_OWNER_UID, ARCHIVE_OWNER_GID]` to `[1000, 1000]` separately so a constant flip cannot move both sides. So the numeric ownership guarantee does NOT depend on the listing at all, and is stated more strictly there than at :66.
The unique value of :66 is therefore narrow and worth keeping in that narrow form: a REAL tar, reading these bytes, reports those ids. Making it format-tolerant costs nothing that :242-243 does not already hold absolutely.

THE OTHER ASSERTIONS IN THAT ARM SURVIVE BOTH FORMATS, and I checked rather than assumed:
- :68-69 splits on `/\r?\n/u` (so bsdtar's CRLF is consumed) and takes `line.split(" ").pop()`, the LAST token, which is the entry name under both layouts despite bsdtar's different column count and date format (`Sep 09 22:33` vs `2026-09-09 22:33`).
- :67 `toContain("-rw-------")` reads the mode from the USTAR header (0600, pinned at :249), not from host file permissions, so both tars should print it. Confirm on the failing host rather than assume — it is the one remaining line in this arm I could not settle from my own tar runs.

SCOPE: `git grep` over the file shows :66 is the ONLY `uid/gid`-format assertion. The docker arm at :128 uses `ls -ln` with `/^-rw-------\s+1\s+1000\s+1000\s/mu`, which is already whitespace-tolerant and is a different tool on a Linux container; it is not affected.

The file is 253 lines and this row touches one line plus a new arm.
planningNotes.risks:
1. A TOLERANT REGEX IS THE WEAKENING DoD 1 FORBIDS, unless it is proven to still reject. `toContain("1000")` or `/1000.*1000/` would pass on uid 1000 / gid 0 — a real delivery failure, since a root-group 0600 file is unreadable by the app user and surfaces 150 seconds later as a health timeout naming nothing. The pattern must require both numbers to be exactly 1000 and ADJACENT, separated only by a slash or spaces, and the negative control is what proves it.

2. DO NOT SUBSTITUTE THE HEADER-FIELD CHECK FOR THIS ARM. :242-243 already carries the numeric guarantee. Deleting :66 in favour of it would lose the only assertion that a REAL tar agrees, which is the file's stated reason for existing (:14-17).

3. `-rw-------` AT :67 IS UNCONFIRMED UNDER bsdtar on the failing host. It should hold, since the mode comes from the USTAR header rather than from host permissions, but I could not settle it with my own scratch archives. If it also fails, it is the same class of defect and belongs in this row — not a new one.

4. THE ARM MUST STILL RUN. `readBack` returns `status: null` when tar is absent; the arm asserts `status === 0` first, so a missing tar reds rather than passes. Keep that ordering — do not restructure the arm so a missing tar becomes a silent skip.
